questions.question: What is the most important mental model for a Beautiful Soup query?
options: It runs against the original HTML string without parsing
It runs against the tree produced by the selected parser
It executes JavaScript before searching for tags
It always sees the same tree regardless of parser
questions.explanation: Beautiful Soup exposes a common search API over a parser-produced tree. Malformed markup may become different trees under different parsers.

questions.question: A product page should contain one optional rating. Which result contract fits select_one()?
options: A Tag or None
A list that is always non-empty
A generator of every matching string
A Boolean that says whether parsing succeeded
questions.explanation: select_one() returns the first matching Tag, or None when there is no match. Calling code must handle the missing case.

questions.question: Why should a deployed extractor specify its parser explicitly?
options: It makes every parser produce browser-identical HTML
It prevents selector methods from returning None
Installed parsers and malformed-markup recovery can differ across environments
It causes Beautiful Soup to download missing parser packages
questions.explanation: An explicit parser makes the tree-building contract repeatable. Otherwise, environment differences can change which parser is selected and which tree selectors see.

questions.question:
For the malformed fragment

, which parser in the lesson applies HTML5 recovery and creates a paragraph inside the anchor?
options: html.parser
lxml's HTML parser
html5lib
SoupStrainer
questions.explanation: For this documented example, html5lib creates a browser-style HTML5 tree and pairs the dangling paragraph close with a new paragraph element.

questions.question: When is SoupStrainer with parse_only most useful?
options: When the job needs only a bounded subset of a large document tree
When JavaScript must run before content appears
When every parser must produce an identical tree
When an HTTP client needs to follow redirects
questions.explanation: SoupStrainer can limit which matching subtrees are built, reducing unnecessary parsing work when the selected parser supports partial parsing.

questions.question: The HTTP response does not contain a price that appears after the page runs JavaScript. What should the extractor do first?
options: Add a broader CSS selector to Beautiful Soup
Retry get_text() until the value appears
Inspect whether an authorized structured endpoint or browser-rendered workflow is required
Switch from find() to find_all()
questions.explanation: Beautiful Soup parses supplied markup; it does not execute page JavaScript. The acquisition layer must obtain the rendered or structured data before parsing.

questions.question: Which change best prevents a support heading from entering a product-title dataset?
options: Use soup.find_all("h2") and discard the last item
Scope the selector to the product boundary, such as article.product > h2
Use soup.select_one("h2")
Convert every heading to lowercase
questions.explanation: A selector should encode the semantic container and expected relationship. Document-order shortcuts are fragile when page structure changes.
